## Game engine (`lib/game/engine/`)

- `GameEngine.ts` — owns `GameState`, processes `dispatch(Command)`, advances `step(dt, input)`, serializes saves, and publishes snapshots (`subscribe`/`getSnapshot`). Randomness is injectable (`rng`) and the world size is overridable for fast headless tests.
- `state.ts` — `GameState` (player with `yaw`/`pitch`, inventory, mobs and thrown
  spears as **logical entities with no Three.js objects**, day clock, mining
  progress, timers) plus `FrameInput`, `GameSnapshot`, `GameEvent`.
- `commands.ts` — the `Command` union: every UI/input mutation enters the simulation through exactly this door.
- `blockChanges.ts` — the delta tracker behind the save format: tracked block writes against the worldgen baseline; reverted edits drop out of the save.
- `systems/` — one module per mechanic, each a function over `GameState`:

### Per-frame step order (in `GameEngine.step`)

0. Pause gate: while `state.paused`, `step` refreshes the snapshot and returns — mobs, the day clock, mining, and stats all freeze (autosave still serializes fine)
1. Stuck detection / auto-unstuck (`STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`)
2. Death check + respawn countdown (while dead, only mobs tick)
3. Sleep gate: while `state.sleepTimer > 0`, `step` decrements the fade and returns (full freeze, like pause); at zero it skips the clock to the next morning
4. Player movement & physics (`systems/playerMotion.ts` — derives direction from `yaw`, scratch vectors, no per-frame allocations)
5. Hunger drain, health regen, continuous-water exposure, lava burn, and oxygen/drowning damage (`systems/playerStats.ts` — `tickWaterExposure`, `tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`, all on the armor-bypassing path)
6. Mining progress and block breaking (`systems/mining.ts`; placement also lives here)
7. Day-night clock (`systems/dayNight.ts` — `daylightAt()` is the single daylight formula); immediately after, `systems/weather.ts` sets the **transient** `state.weather` (rain/snow/clear) as a pure function of `dayClock` + seed — cosmetic only: never serialized, never touches spawn/daylight balance
8. Random block ticks (`systems/randomTicks.ts` — each interval samples columns near the player and runs per-block handlers; drives crop growth and is the extension point for future saplings / grass spread)
9. Night hostile spawning (`systems/spawnDirector.ts`, interval/cap in config)
10. Dungeon spawners (`systems/spawnDirector.ts` `tickSpawnerDirector` — each interval, every intact dungeon spawner with the player in range drips one hostile onto the room floor, bounded by a local cluster cap and the shared `HOSTILE_CAP`; time-independent)
11. Mob AI: wander/aggro/flee, attacks with line-of-sight, daylight burn (`systems/mobAI.ts`). Ranged mobs (skeletons, boss) kite and loose arrows instead of meleeing; the boss also bears down, melees up close, fires a spread, and summons minions
12. Projectiles (`systems/projectileAI.ts` `tickProjectiles` — arrows integrate under gravity in capped substeps; block hits reuse the swept world DDA and the entity test is substepped so fast arrows can't tunnel; spent arrows despawn). Also ticked in the dead branch so in-flight arrows clear
13. Animal breeding (`systems/breeding.ts` — feed-to-love timers, baby maturity, pairing in-love adults within range; the passive cap bounds the population)

**Projectiles** are session-only entities (`ProjectileState` in `state.ts`, spawned via `projectiles.ts` `spawnArrow`), never serialized — like mobs. A `fromPlayer` flag is the hit filter: player arrows (the bow) hit mobs with knockback, mob arrows hit the player (armor-mitigated), and neither hits the firer. The bow, ranged skeletons, and the boss all share this one launch path. Thrown **spears** are a parallel transient entity (`ThrownSpearState`, `systems/spears.ts`) with their own gravity, swept mob collision, and terrain raycasts.

62	**Game modes.** The four modes (`survival`/`creative`/`adventure`/`spectator`, `lib/game/gameModes.ts`) are a single `state.gameMode` axis. Systems gate on **intent predicates** rather than the raw id, so all four share one set of seams: `takesDamage` switches off the three damage chokepoints in `playerLife.ts` (covering fall/void/lava/water/drown/mob/poison at once) plus hunger/regen/oxygen in `playerStats.ts`; `canEditBlocks`/`freeBuild` gate breaking and placing in `mining.ts`; `canInteract` gates the interaction commands in `dispatch`; `canFly`/`isNoclip` drive flight and the collision skip in `playerMotion.ts` (and the auto-unstuck skip in `step`); `mobsThreaten` folds into `activeHostile` in `mobAI.ts`; `usesInventory`/`takesDamage` hide HUD elements. `gameMode` rides the per-world `worldType` plumbing (`WorldMeta` → a v8 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`), but unlike `worldType` it's **switchable in-game** — `setGameMode` (`GameEngine.switchGameMode`) resets transient hazard timers, bars, flight, and noclip-entombment on the change. The transient `isFlying` is never serialized.
63	
64	**Difficulty.** Orthogonal to the mode, `state.difficulty` (`peaceful`/`easy`/`normal`/`hard`, `lib/game/difficulties.ts`) decides _how hard_ survival is — it follows the same shape as game modes: an enum, an `isDifficulty` guard, `DIFFICULTY_PRESETS` for the UI, and **accessor functions** (`hostilesSpawn`, `mobDamageMultiplier`, `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`, `hostileCapScale`, `regenIntervalScale`, `starves`/`starvationFloorHp`) that systems read instead of the raw id. The seams: `spawnDirector.ts` gates the initial population + night director + dungeon spawners on `hostilesSpawn` and scales the cadence/cap; `mobAI.ts` multiplies every mob hit at the strike (templates untouched); `playerStats.ts` scales regen and runs the new **starvation** tick (hunger 0 chips to a per-level HP floor, lethal only on Hard, routed through the same floored/lethal damage paths as Poison/environment). Difficulty rides the same per-world plumbing as `gameMode` (`WorldMeta` → a v9 `SaveData` field → `GameEngine`) and is switchable in-game — `setDifficulty` (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`) just updates the value the directors read next tick, except dropping to Peaceful, which despawns the hostiles already present (a plain splice — no loot/XP, no false boss victory). The two axes don't cross-couple: spawning keys only on difficulty, threat/damage only on mode.
65	
66	**Hardcore.** A per-world boolean (`state.hardcore`, persisted in save v10 + `WorldMeta`, **immutable** unlike mode/difficulty). The constructor resolves it first so it overrides the other axes — forced to Survival + Hard — and `switchGameMode`/`switchDifficulty` early-return under it (the player-facing switchers are disabled; the engine's own death transition sets the mode directly, bypassing the lock). Death is permanent: the two lethal seams (`applyDamage`, `applyEnvironmentalDamage`) divert to `GameEngine.triggerGameOver()`, which sets the persisted `gameOver` flag and flips the player to **Spectator** (a free-cam over the dead world, invulnerable so mobs can't re-trigger it) instead of arming the respawn countdown — so a reloaded `gameOver` world boots straight into spectating (the constructor resolves `gameMode` to spectator; the existing `!isNoclip` stuck-check leaves it un-teleported). The shell force-saves on the `gameOver` event so a tab-close still persists the dead world; the Game Over screen (`components/game/GameOverScreen.tsx`) owns navigation (spectate / quit / delete), and `pause` is blocked while `gameOver`. The hearts render in a withered palette (`lib/ui/hudPixels.ts`).
67	
68	Combat (`systems/combat.ts`) runs on the `attack` command rather than per frame: a held bow branches to `tryFireBow` (instant click-to-fire, no draw-charge), a spear melees at its longer `weaponReach`, and otherwise `tryAttackMob` swings. The `placeBlock` command runs a fixed right-click precedence (`systems/interact.ts` + engine): throw the selected spear (`tryThrowSelectedSpear`) → feed an aimed animal (`tryFeedAimedMob`) → interact with the aimed block (`tryInteractBlock`, e.g. bed/furnace/chest/door) → summon the boss from a Cursed Totem (`trySummonBoss`) → use the held item (`tryUseHeldItem`, e.g. hoe tills soil, seeds plant a crop) → `placeSelectedBlock` — so each interaction consumes the click instead of getting a block placed against it. New mechanics get a new system module and a slot in this sequence — don't grow the engine class with inline logic.
69

1	# Testing
2	
3	Two runners, three layers:
4	
5	- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover. The shared setup (`tests/setup.ts`, preloaded via `bunfig.toml`) registers happy-dom so React component tests run under the same runner; the game engine itself needs no DOM (see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).
6	- **`bun run test:e2e`** — Playwright browser smoke tests in `e2e/*.e2e.ts` against the production build. The file suffix matters: `bun test` auto-collects `*.test.ts` AND `*.spec.ts`, so E2E files must use `.e2e.ts`.
7

## What

Adds the missing **progression meta** to Monecraft. After three combat/gear releases (#35/#36/#37) the game was content-rich but goal-poor — the only objective was "beat the Dragon Lord." This gives players a guided tour of every system and a running record of what they've done:

- **Statistics** — running counters: blocks mined, monsters slain, items crafted/enchanted, potions drunk, fish caught, animals bred, distance travelled, time played, deaths, jumps, villager trades.
- **Advancements** — a tight, flat set of **16** achievements, one per major system (mine a log/stone/sliver/diamond, craft a pickaxe, craft a furnace, fire a bow, slay a hostile, defeat the Dragon Lord, breed animals, harvest wheat, catch a fish, enchant an item, drink a potion, sleep, trade with a villager). Each unlocks the moment its goal is met, with a toast + chime.

Both surface in a dedicated **`L`-key overlay** (two tabs), **persist in the save and survive death** (like `xp`, unlike `effects`), and add **zero binary assets** — advancement icons reuse existing item/block sprites.

## How

- **One chokepoint.** Every gameplay event already funnels through `GameEngine.emit`. A single observer there folds each event into the stat counters (`recordEvent`) and unlocks any advancement whose threshold the new stats just crossed (`evaluateAdvancements` → `advancementUnlocked`) — no per-system bookkeeping. The advancement set is a **declarative `{ stat, threshold }` registry** in `lib/game/engine/systems/advancements.ts`, so adding one is a one-line edit.
- A new broadly-useful **`crafted` event** drives the craft/brew/trade counters. `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` (`lib/game/mobs.ts`) is the single source of truth for counting hostile kills (hostility isn't stored on `MOB_TEMPLATES`).
- **Persistence:** save **v12 → v13** (additive, pure migration). `WORLDGEN_VERSION` stays 8; `SAVE_KEY` unchanged.
- **UI:** the `L` key mirrors the inventory handler; the two full-screen overlays are mutually exclusive and the pause menu won't open over either. The panel reads detail through a new `GameApi.advancementState()` pulled on render, so play never churns the snapshot with stat values the HUD doesn't show. A celebratory ZZFX chime plays on unlock.

## Commits

1. `feat(stats): track gameplay statistics`
2. `feat(advancements): registry + unlock tracking`
3. `feat(ui): advancements & statistics overlay (L key)`
4. `docs(advancements): document advancements & statistics`

Done. The **Advancements + Statistics** feature is implemented end-to-end on `feat/advancements`, pushed, and opened as **[PR #38](https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/38)** against `hutusi/main`.

## What shipped (4 focused commits)

| Commit | Scope |
|---|---|
| `feat(stats)` | `state.stats` Map + `recordEvent`/`recordTick` + `STATS` + `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` + the new `crafted` event + save **v12→v13** persistence of stats |
| `feat(advancements)` | 16-entry declarative `ADVANCEMENTS` registry + the emit-chokepoint observer + `advancementUnlocked` event + `advancements` Set persistence |
| `feat(ui)` | `L`-key handler, `toggleAdvancements` command, `GameApi.advancementState()`, the two-tab `AdvancementsPanel` + CSS, the unlock toast + a new ZZFX chime |
| `docs` | manual, reference (advancement + stats tables), save-format (v13), adding-content (extension pattern), architecture (emit-observer note), testing (coverage), CHANGELOG |

## Design highlights
- **One chokepoint, zero per-system edits** — every event already flows through `GameEngine.emit`; a single observer there records stats and unlocks advancements.
- **Declarative registry** — each advancement is a `{ stat, threshold }` row, so `evaluateAdvancements` is pure and adding one is a one-liner.
- **Death-proof persistence** — stats + advancements survive death like `xp` (unlike `effects`), verified by a round-trip-then-die engine test.
- **Zero binary assets** — icons reuse existing item/block sprites.

## Verification (full CI gate green)
`lint` · `typecheck` · `format:check` · **`bun test` 900 pass** · `build` · **`bun run test:e2e` 18/18** (incl. a new test: press `L` → opens → shows the unlocked entry → switches tabs → closes).

The three plan refinements all held up: `HOSTILE_MOB_KINDS` replaced the non-existent `MOB_TEMPLATES.hostile`, the `crafted` event drives the trade/craft counters, and `itemIconUrl` rendered the block-id icons fine.

**One thing left to you:** a quick manual gameplay pass — the overlay layout/icons and the unlock toast + chime aren't headless-verifiable. Everything else is covered by tests. CodeRabbit review on the PR is still pending.

===== INLINE REVIEW COMMENTS (actionable findings) =====
── lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:257
_🗄️ Data Integrity & Integration_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Filter restored advancement ids against the registry.**

`restoreAdvancements()` only guarantees “non-empty string”, so a corrupt/manual-edited save can inject arbitrary ids into `state.advancements`. Because the snapshot publishes `state.advancements.size` directly, those bogus ids inflate the unlocked count and get written back out forever on the next save.

```diff
-      for (const id of restoreAdvancements(save)) this.state.advancements.add(id);
+      for (const id of restoreAdvancements(save)) {
+        if (ADVANCEMENTS_BY_ID[id]) this.state.advancements.add(id);
+      }
```
</details>

fix(advancements): address code review

CodeRabbit review on PR #38 — five findings, all applied:

- **Hardcore deaths now count** (Major): the permadeath path emits `gameOver`,
  not `died`, so `recordEvent` undercounted deaths in hardcore runs. It now
  treats `gameOver` as a death too (exactly one of the two fires per death, so
  no double-count).
- **Stats tab stays current** (Major): the overlay pulls data on render, but the
  snapshot only changed on an unlock, so continuous counters (play time,
  distance) could read stale. `MinecraftGame` now re-renders on a light interval
  *while the overlay is open* — keeping stat freshness off the hot per-frame
  snapshot path (a per-frame snapshot version field would reintroduce exactly the
  churn the design avoids).
- **Restored advancements are registry-filtered** (Minor): a corrupt/edited save
  could inject bogus ids that inflated the unlocked count and round-tripped
  forever; the restore loop now keeps only ids in the registry.
- **`items_crafted` is workbench crafts only** (Minor): it was bumping for every
  `crafted` event including smelting/brewing/trading; those have their own
  counters, so the displayed "Items Crafted" no longer folds them in.
- **`flashMessage` cancels its prior clear timer** (Minor): toasts arriving in a
  burst (an unlock alongside a pickup/autosave toast) could clear each other
  early; the helper now replaces the active clear timer instead of stacking them.
EOF
